page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-80 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on 64-bit Intel x86_64 architecture. It provides 80 dedicated virtual CPUs across 40 physical processor cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 320 GB of system memory, matching a standard balanced profile of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU, supported by 260 MB of shared L3 cache. It includes no bundled local storage and no discrete graphics processing units, relying entirely on network-attached storage volumes for persistent data needs.

Benchmark testing demonstrates strong multi-core computational capabilities alongside average single-core performance. The instance achieved top-tier throughput in static web serving at 95.08 GB/sec and strong multi-core results in stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations. Support for advanced vector and matrix instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, delivers robust throughput in parallel mathematical tasks and CPU-based inference. High uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 276 GB/sec for reads and 123 GB/sec for writes complements in-memory processing, evidenced by 88.02 million operations per second in Redis SET testing.

From an efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-80 delivers high compute and memory capacity in a single virtual instance, minimizing multi-node coordination overhead for parallel systems. However, users must account for the lack of local NVMe storage and average single-thread execution speeds when planning workloads. The configuration is suitable for scale-out web serving tiers, multi-threaded software compilation, distributed caching nodes, batch ETL operations, and container orchestration workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-80 is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 80 dedicated vCPUs derived from 40 physical Intel x86_64 cores and 320 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance features 260 MB of L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets for accelerated vector and matrix math. Without bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, persistent storage relies on external network disks. In benchmark evaluations, the n4-standard-80 demonstrates strong multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth, achieving 95.08 GB/sec in static web serving and 88.02 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, contrasted with average single-core performance. Its balanced resource profile makes it cost-efficient for parallel enterprise workloads, continuous integration compilation pipelines, distributed caching clusters, high-traffic web applications, and CPU-based model inference.
